Two reasons that are both related to performance:

  1. Vote calculations (we can not continue to count every vote every time a user logs in, it's too much data to scan).
  2. Submission views. When we archive data we can effectively mark these as not part of the result set for certain queries like hot. If we didn't we have the same problem as #1.
Thought it was something like that. Is it possible to make some in between solution that would enable commenting on old threads, but no voting and no queries and not cause a performance hit?

Ideally we wouldn't "archive" any data but this is simply impossible in the grand scheme of things.

And yes, we have an idea on how we can archive but still allow new content. Unfortunately this is not a priority right now. In the future we will most likely have all archiving based simply on creation dates such that anything that is older than x is frozen but new content can be appended an thus have it's own date range independent of the context data.

At least that is our plan when we have time to get to it.
